title: Clustered integer execution units with duplicated register files
decision: Split the integer register file into two clusters, each with a duplicated 80-entry register file and two pipelines, supporting four-way integer execution
alternatives_or_rejected: An idealized unclustered implementation with a single larger register file
rationale: Clustering makes the design simpler and faster, although it costs an extra cycle of latency to broadcast results from one integer cluster to the other; performance cost of clustering and issue-queue arbitration simplifications is small (a few percent or less)
outcome: Four integer pipes (upper/lower in each of two clusters); most dependent computations stay on the same cluster; cross-cluster result broadcast costs one extra cycle
quote_as_recalled: This clustering makes the design simpler and faster, although it costs an extra cycle of latency to broadcast results from an integer cluster to the other cluster.
weakest_point: Exact page number and precise wording of the 'few percent' claim

title: Line and way prediction for set-associative instruction cache
where_in_paper: Instruction pipeline—Fetch / line and way prediction
decision: Use a 64-Kbyte two-way set-associative instruction cache together with line and way prediction so that the next fetch block (including which way) is predicted and accessed with direct-mapped speed
alternatives_or_rejected: A pure direct-mapped instruction cache (as in the prior 21164 8-Kbyte design) or a conventional set-associative access that would lengthen the critical fetch path
rationale: Combines the advantages of set-associative behavior and fetch-bubble elimination with the fast access time of a direct-mapped cache; address paths needing extra logic (decode, branch prediction, tag compare) stay outside the critical fetch loop
outcome: Line/way predictors correct ~95-100% of the time for most applications; most mispredictions cost only a single cycle; improved L1 hit rates versus the 21164 while preserving high-frequency fetch
quote_as_recalled: a line and way prediction technique that combines the advantages of set-associative behavior and fetch bubble elimination, together with the fast access time of a direct-mapped cache
weakest_point: Exact hit-rate percentage recalled from the paper

title: Tournament branch predictor combining local and global history
decision: Implement a tournament branch predictor that dynamically chooses, for each branch, between a local-history predictor and a global-history predictor
alternatives_or_rejected: Larger tables of either local-history-only or global-history-only predictors
rationale: The combination yields better prediction accuracy than larger tables of either individual method; the processor adapts to choose the best method for each branch
outcome: 90-100% success rate on most simulated applications/benchmarks; local predictor uses 10-bit histories for up to 1024 branches feeding 1024 counters; global uses 4096-entry tables indexed by 12-bit path history
quote_as_recalled: The result is a tournament branch predictor with better prediction accuracy than larger tables of either individual method
weakest_point: Exact table sizes and success-rate numbers

title: Out-of-order execution with map stage and larger in-flight window
decision: Add a map (rename) stage and support out-of-order speculative execution allowing up to 80 in-flight instructions (versus 20 on the prior 21164)
alternatives_or_rejected: Continuing with the in-order pipeline style of the 21164
rationale: Instructions execute as soon as possible and in parallel with other nondependent work; critical-path computations start and complete quickly; more functional units plus dynamic techniques extract greater parallelism even though both generations fetch at most four instructions per cycle
outcome: Processor is 50% to 200% faster than the 21164 for many applications; seven-stage pipeline similar to 21164 but with the added map stage fundamental to out-of-order techniques
quote_as_recalled: One notable addition is the map stage that renames registers to expose instruction parallelism—this addition is fundamental to the 21264’s out-of-order techniques.
weakest_point: Exact in-flight instruction count attribution to this paper versus related papers

title: Larger two-way associative on-chip data cache
decision: Implement a 64-Kbyte two-way set-associative data cache (versus the prior generation’s smaller direct-mapped cache)
alternatives_or_rejected: The 8-Kbyte direct-mapped data cache used in the 21164
rationale: Much lower miss rates than the earlier design, contributing to a high-bandwidth, low-latency memory system that can service many parallel references
outcome: Cache can support any combination of two loads or stores per cycle (double-pumped); tracks up to 32 in-flight loads, 32 stores and 8 cache misses; sustains >1.3 GBytes/s on Stream
quote_as_recalled: This cache has much lower miss rates than the 8-Kbyte, direct-mapped cache in the earlier 21164.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly frames the size/associativity choice as a weighed alternative versus other capacity points
